description: Design a business dashboard from audience analysis through layout and refresh cadence.

steps.description: Identify the dashboard audience and the decisions they make.

inputs.name: stakeholder-list
inputs.desc: List of people who will use the dashboard

inputs.name: business-context
inputs.desc: Description of the business area the dashboard covers

outputs.name: audience-profile
outputs.desc: Who the users are and what decisions they need to make

outputs.name: information-needs
outputs.desc: What questions the dashboard must answer for each audience

process: List each stakeholder group and their role.
For each group, identify the decisions they make weekly or monthly.
Map each decision to the information needed to make it.

steps.description: Select the KPIs and metrics to display on the dashboard.

inputs.name: audience-profile
inputs.desc: Who the users are and their decisions

inputs.name: information-needs
inputs.desc: What questions the dashboard must answer

outputs.name: selected-metrics
outputs.desc: List of metrics with definitions, data sources, and update frequency

outputs.name: metric-hierarchy
outputs.desc: How the metrics relate to each other (primary, secondary, supporting)

process: For each information need, identify the metric that answers it.
Define each metric: name, formula, data source, update frequency.
Rank metrics into primary (top of dashboard), secondary, and supporting.
Verify that every audience decision maps to at least one metric.

steps.description: Design the dashboard layout including grouping, visual types, and hierarchy.

outputs.name: layout-wireframe
outputs.desc: Dashboard layout showing placement of each metric and visual type

outputs.name: visual-type-map
outputs.desc: Which chart or visual type to use for each metric

process: Group metrics by theme or business area.
Assign a visual type to each metric (number tile, line chart, bar chart, table).
Arrange groups on the layout with primary metrics at the top.
Add filters, date selectors, and drill-down paths.

steps.description: Choose the visualization tool and set the refresh cadence.

outputs.name: tool-selection
outputs.desc: Chosen visualization platform with rationale

outputs.name: refresh-schedule
outputs.desc: How often each data source refreshes

process: Evaluate available tools against the visual types and data sources needed.
Select the tool and document the rationale.
Set the refresh cadence for each data source (real-time, hourly, daily).

steps.description: Build the dashboard and validate it against the original requirements.

outputs.name: dashboard-artifact
outputs.desc: The built dashboard ready for use

outputs.name: dashboard-design-doc
outputs.desc: Documentation of the dashboard design decisions and maintenance plan

process: Build the dashboard in the chosen tool following the wireframe.
Connect the data sources and verify the refresh schedule.
Walk through the dashboard with a sample user from each audience group.
Document the design decisions and set a review schedule.

description: Automate recurring reports from manual processes to scheduled delivery.

steps.description: Inventory all current manual reports and their characteristics.

inputs.name: report-owners
inputs.desc: People who currently produce manual reports

inputs.name: report-scope
inputs.desc: Which department or function to audit

outputs.name: report-catalog
outputs.desc: List of reports with frequency, audience, data sources, and time to produce

outputs.name: automation-candidates
outputs.desc: Reports ranked by automation potential (frequency times effort)

process: Interview each report owner about what they produce, how often, and how long it takes.
Catalog each report: name, frequency, audience, data sources, format, production time.
Rank by automation potential: high-frequency and high-effort reports first.

steps.description: Build the automated data pipeline for the report.

outputs.name: data-pipeline-spec
outputs.desc: Specification of the automated data extraction and transformation

outputs.name: pipeline-validation
outputs.desc: Comparison of automated output against the last manual report

process: For the top candidate, map the data sources and transformations.
Build the extraction and transformation pipeline.
Run the pipeline and compare output against the most recent manual report.
Fix any discrepancies until the outputs match.

steps.description: Design the automated report template and schedule delivery.

inputs.name: data-pipeline-spec
inputs.desc: How the data is extracted and transformed

outputs.name: report-template
outputs.desc: The report template with placeholders for automated data

outputs.name: delivery-schedule
outputs.desc: When and how each report is generated and distributed

process: Design the report template matching the current format.
Connect the template to the data pipeline.
Set the generation schedule and distribution list.
Test end-to-end: trigger, generate, deliver.

steps.description: Validate the automated reports and produce the setup document.

outputs.name: validation-results
outputs.desc: Comparison of automated output against manual for three cycles

outputs.name: automation-setup-doc
outputs.desc: Documentation of the automated reporting system

process: Run the automated report in parallel with the manual report for three cycles.
Compare outputs and resolve any differences.
Document the setup, including how to modify the report and troubleshoot failures.

description: Define data visualization standards for an organization.

steps.description: Audit current visualizations across the organization for consistency.

inputs.name: dashboard-inventory
inputs.desc: List of existing dashboards and reports with visualizations

inputs.name: brand-guidelines
inputs.desc: Existing brand guidelines (colors, fonts) if available

outputs.name: audit-findings
outputs.desc: Inconsistencies found across current visualizations

outputs.name: pattern-catalog
outputs.desc: Common patterns and anti-patterns observed

process: Collect screenshots or links from all existing dashboards and reports.
Catalog the chart types, colors, fonts, and labeling patterns in use.
Identify inconsistencies and common mistakes.

steps.description: Define which chart type to use for each data scenario.

outputs.name: chart-type-guidelines
outputs.desc: When to use each chart type (bar, line, pie, scatter, table, tile)

outputs.name: anti-pattern-list
outputs.desc: Common visualization mistakes to avoid

process: Define the data scenarios: comparison, trend, proportion, distribution, relationship.
Assign the correct chart type to each scenario with examples.
Document anti-patterns with before/after corrections.

steps.description: Set the color palette and typography rules for data visualizations.

outputs.name: color-palette
outputs.desc: Sequential, diverging, and categorical color palettes for data

outputs.name: typography-rules
outputs.desc: Font sizes and weights for titles, labels, annotations, and values

process: Define a categorical palette (6 to 8 distinct colors) aligned with the brand.
Define sequential and diverging palettes for quantitative data.
Set typography rules: title size, axis label size, annotation size, value display.

steps.description: Compile and publish the visualization standards guide.

outputs.name: visualization-standards-guide
outputs.desc: Complete standards document with examples

outputs.name: template-library
outputs.desc: Starter templates implementing the standards

process: Compile all rules, palettes, and examples into a single document.
Create starter templates in the most-used visualization tools.
Distribute to the organization and set a review cadence.

description: Build a shared SQL query library from common ad-hoc queries.

steps.description: Inventory the most common ad-hoc SQL queries across the team.

inputs.name: analyst-team
inputs.desc: List of analysts who write SQL queries

outputs.name: query-inventory
outputs.desc: Collection of commonly written queries with frequency and purpose

outputs.name: duplication-map
outputs.desc: Queries that multiple people write for the same purpose

process: Collect the most frequently run queries from each analyst.
Categorize by purpose: revenue, usage, retention, operations, support.
Identify duplicates where multiple people wrote the same query differently.

steps.description: Write standardized, tested versions of each query.

outputs.name: standardized-queries
outputs.desc: Clean, tested, documented queries

outputs.name: test-results
outputs.desc: Validation that each query returns expected results

process: For each unique purpose, write one canonical query.
Add parameters for common variations (date range, segment, region).
Test each query against known data and verify results.
Add performance notes (expected runtime, index usage).

steps.description: Organize the queries into a versioned, searchable library.

outputs.name: query-library
outputs.desc: Organized library with categories, search, and documentation

outputs.name: library-maintenance-plan
outputs.desc: How to add, update, and retire queries

process: Organize queries into categories matching the business domains.
Document each query: purpose, parameters, expected output, performance.
Set up version control and a process for adding new queries.
Publish the library to the team.

description: Define and govern business metrics for an organization.

steps.description: Identify the key business questions that metrics must answer.

inputs.name: stakeholder-interviews
inputs.desc: Input from leaders about what they need to measure

outputs.name: business-questions
outputs.desc: Prioritized list of questions the business needs answered

outputs.name: measurement-gaps
outputs.desc: Questions that currently have no metric

process: Review the business objectives and strategy.
Interview stakeholders about the questions they ask most often.
Prioritize questions by impact and frequency.
Identify which questions have no current metric.

steps.description: Define each metric with its formula, source, owner, and update frequency.

outputs.name: metric-definitions
outputs.desc: Each metric with name, formula, data source, owner, update frequency

outputs.name: metric-targets
outputs.desc: Targets and thresholds for each metric

process: For each question, define the metric: name, formula, data source, owner.
Set the update frequency (real-time, daily, weekly, monthly).
Set targets and thresholds (green, yellow, red).
Document the lineage from raw data to the metric.

steps.description: Publish the metrics dictionary and set the governance process.

outputs.name: metrics-dictionary
outputs.desc: Published reference document of all business metrics

outputs.name: metrics-governance-plan
outputs.desc: Process for adding, changing, and retiring metrics

process: Compile all definitions into a searchable dictionary.
Define the governance process: how to propose, approve, and retire metrics.
Distribute the dictionary to the organization.
Set a quarterly review cadence.

description: Set up self-service analytics for business users.

steps.description: Assess business user needs and skill levels for self-service analytics.

inputs.name: user-groups
inputs.desc: Business teams that need analytics access

outputs.name: needs-assessment
outputs.desc: What each user group needs to do with data

outputs.name: skill-levels
outputs.desc: Current data literacy by group (beginner, intermediate, advanced)

process: Survey each user group about their current data questions and how they answer them.
Assess the data literacy level of each group.
Identify the gap between what they need and what they can do today.

steps.description: Select the analytics platform and prepare the data layer.

outputs.name: platform-selection
outputs.desc: Chosen analytics platform with rationale

outputs.name: data-layer-spec
outputs.desc: Semantic model and curated datasets for self-service use

process: Evaluate platforms against user needs and skill levels.
Select the platform and document the rationale.
Design the data layer: semantic model, curated datasets, pre-built dimensions and measures.

steps.description: Build starter dashboards and train users.

outputs.name: starter-dashboards
outputs.desc: Pre-built dashboards and templates for each user group

outputs.name: training-plan
outputs.desc: Training materials and schedule

process: Build starter dashboards addressing the top questions for each user group.
Create templates users can copy and modify.
Write training materials matched to each skill level.
Schedule training sessions and set up a support channel.

steps.description: Produce the self-service analytics plan and adoption tracking.

outputs.name: self-service-plan
outputs.desc: Complete plan for self-service analytics rollout

outputs.name: adoption-metrics
outputs.desc: How to measure whether users are adopting self-service analytics

process: Document the rollout plan: timeline, user groups, milestones.
Define adoption metrics: active users, queries run, dashboards created.
Set a review cadence to track adoption and adjust.

description: Build a data story from analysis through presentation.

steps.description: Define the audience and the question being answered.

inputs.name: analysis-request
inputs.desc: What question or problem the analysis addresses

inputs.name: target-audience
inputs.desc: Who will receive the data story

outputs.name: audience-context
outputs.desc: What the audience knows, what they care about, what action they can take

outputs.name: core-question
outputs.desc: The single question the data story will answer

process: Identify who the audience is and what decisions they can make.
State the core question in one sentence.
Note what the audience already knows so the story does not repeat it.

steps.description: Conduct the analysis and identify the key insight.

outputs.name: key-insight
outputs.desc: The single most important finding

outputs.name: supporting-evidence
outputs.desc: Data points that support the key insight

process: Conduct the analysis to answer the core question.
Identify the single most important finding.
Gather the supporting data points that make the case.
Test the insight: would the audience be surprised or act differently because of it?

steps.description: Structure the narrative using situation, complication, resolution.

outputs.name: narrative-outline
outputs.desc: Story arc: situation, complication, resolution

outputs.name: visual-plan
outputs.desc: Which charts and visuals support each part of the narrative

process: Write the situation: what the audience expects or assumes.
Write the complication: what the data shows that challenges or confirms the assumption.
Write the resolution: what action the insight suggests.
Plan the visuals: one chart per key point, no more.

steps.description: Design the visuals and produce the data story presentation.

outputs.name: data-story-presentation
outputs.desc: Finished presentation or document with the data story

outputs.name: executive-summary
outputs.desc: One-paragraph summary of the insight and recommended action

process: Build each visual following the narrative order.
Add annotations that guide the reader to the insight.
Write the executive summary: insight, evidence, recommended action.
Review the story end to end: does it answer the core question?

description: Set up a framework for handling ad-hoc analysis requests.

steps.description: Define the intake process for ad-hoc analysis requests.

outputs.name: intake-form
outputs.desc: Standardized request form with required fields

outputs.name: triage-criteria
outputs.desc: How to classify requests by urgency and complexity

process: Define who can submit requests and through what channel.
Design the intake form: question, context, deadline, decisions it supports.
Set triage criteria: urgent (same day), standard (this week), research (this month).

steps.description: Assign requests to analysts and set expectations.

outputs.name: assignment-rules
outputs.desc: How requests are matched to analysts based on skill and availability

outputs.name: turnaround-slas
outputs.desc: Expected turnaround time by request type

process: Match request types to analyst skills.
Set turnaround expectations by triage level.
Define the handoff protocol between requestor and analyst.

steps.description: Deliver the analysis and log the request for tracking.

outputs.name: delivery-protocol
outputs.desc: How finished analyses are delivered and presented

outputs.name: ad-hoc-analysis-framework-doc
outputs.desc: Complete framework document covering intake, triage, assignment, delivery, and logging

process: Define the delivery format (document, dashboard, presentation).
Set up a log to track all requests, assignments, delivery dates, and outcomes.
Compile the full framework into a document.
Review the log monthly for patterns that suggest a recurring report should replace ad-hoc requests.

description: Set up executive reporting from audience definition through production schedule.

steps.description: Define the executive reporting audience and their information needs.

inputs.name: executive-team
inputs.desc: List of executives who receive reports

inputs.name: reporting-context
inputs.desc: Current state of executive reporting (what exists, what is missing)

outputs.name: audience-needs
outputs.desc: What each executive needs to see and how often

outputs.name: report-inventory
outputs.desc: Existing reports mapped to audience needs, with gaps identified

process: List each executive and their area of responsibility.
Identify what decisions they make and what information they need.
Map existing reports to these needs and identify gaps.

steps.description: Design the report format and select the metrics.

outputs.name: report-designs
outputs.desc: Format and metrics for each report (one-page summary, dashboard, or deck)

outputs.name: production-schedule
outputs.desc: When each report is produced and delivered

process: For each gap, design the report format: one-page summary, dashboard, or slide deck.
Select the metrics for each report from the metrics dictionary.
Set the production schedule: who produces it, when, and how it is delivered.

steps.description: Launch the reporting cadence and set the review process.

outputs.name: reporting-cadence-doc
outputs.desc: Complete executive reporting plan

outputs.name: review-process
outputs.desc: How and when to review and update the reporting cadence

process: Produce the first cycle of each report.
Gather feedback from the executive audience.
Adjust formats and metrics based on feedback.
Document the cadence and set a quarterly review.

description: Conduct a cohort analysis from definition through visualization and insight extraction.

steps.description: Define the cohort criteria and analysis parameters.

inputs.name: analysis-question
inputs.desc: What question the cohort analysis should answer

inputs.name: available-data
inputs.desc: What data is available for cohort grouping

outputs.name: cohort-definition
outputs.desc: How users are grouped into cohorts (signup date, first purchase, plan tier)

outputs.name: analysis-parameters
outputs.desc: Time periods, metric to track (retention, conversion, revenue), granularity

process: State the question: are we retaining users better over time? Is a specific segment converting differently?
Define the cohort grouping: by week, month, acquisition channel, or plan tier.
Set the metric to track and the time granularity (weekly, monthly).

steps.description: Pull and prepare the cohort data.

inputs.name: analysis-parameters
inputs.desc: What to measure and at what granularity

outputs.name: cohort-dataset
outputs.desc: Structured data with cohort, time period, and metric value

outputs.name: data-quality-notes
outputs.desc: Any issues with the data (missing periods, small cohorts)

process: Write and run the query to pull user-level data with cohort assignments.
Aggregate to the cohort and time period level.
Check for data quality issues: missing periods, cohorts with fewer than 30 users.

steps.description: Visualize the cohort table and identify patterns.

outputs.name: cohort-table
outputs.desc: Formatted cohort table (heatmap or triangle chart)

outputs.name: pattern-observations
outputs.desc: Trends and outliers identified in the data

process: Build the cohort table as a heatmap with color intensity showing the metric.
Identify trends: are newer cohorts performing better or worse?
Identify outliers: any cohort or time period that deviates from the pattern.

steps.description: Extract insights and produce the cohort analysis report.

outputs.name: cohort-insights
outputs.desc: Key findings from the analysis with supporting data

outputs.name: cohort-analysis-report
outputs.desc: Complete report with methodology, findings, and recommendations

process: State the key finding in one sentence.
Support it with specific cohort comparisons.
Recommend actions based on the findings.
Compile into the analysis report.
